camera: Orthographic projection: edges stay parallel and nothing converges. Measured on stall-full.png (420px wide), the grass patch's left edge runs at a slope of about 0.52 (27.5 deg on screen) and its right edge at about 0.58 (30 deg). That puts the view between 2:1 dimetric (26.6 deg) and true isometric (30 deg). Use azimuth 45 deg to the base axes and elevation 30-33 deg, i.e. dir = normalize(sin45*cos30, sin30, cos45*cos30), with no roll. In the fishing scene the camera is the same but the pier is turned about 15-20 deg in the scene, so its long axis reads at about 18 deg on screen instead of 27-30 deg. Ripple rings are flattened to an aspect of about 0.5, which is a true circle on the ground seen from about 30 deg elevation. Framing: a square 1:1 frame. The diorama is centered horizontally and fills about 85% of the width, leaving about 7-8% white on each side. Vertically it sits slightly low: about 25-30% white above (the roof and pole end well below the top) and about 15-20% below. The frame has no horizon, no sky and no floor, only the object on white. The camera does not move.
pixelation: This is fine pixel art, not chunky. In the 420px-wide captures, the dither checker alternates every pixel: one row at the water edge reads F4/C3/F3/D0/EC in grayscale. Grass blades and the fishing line are also 1px wide. One art-pixel is therefore about 1/360 to 1/420 of the frame width, and the diorama is about 300-350 art-pixels across. Render at about 384x384 and scale up with nearest-neighbour by an integer factor (x3 to 1152, or x2.8 for 1080). The intended result is hard-edged: stair-stepped silhouettes, 1px stair-stepping on thin lines (the fishing line and rod look dashed), and no anti-aliasing. The softness in the references is video compression, not filtering. Use NearestFilter on the target, antialias:false, setPixelRatio(1) and CSS image-rendering:pixelated. Small objects are only a few dozen art-pixels: a person is about 22-28px tall, a pot about 8px and the bike about 30px.
outlines:
There are no ink outlines and no Sobel or depth-edge lines. Silhouettes meet the white directly: the light straw roof edge (#E4D1A8 against #FFFFFF) and the light water edge have no dark rim at all. Edges are defined only by value contrast:
- very dark, cool undersides and side faces (pier posts and under-deck #161B20-#303E49, the stall interior under the roof #4F3428);
- the dark gaps between grass blades.
Thin structures (bike frame and basket wires, chair frame, fishing rod and line, banner pole) are simply 1-art-px geometry in a darker or lighter tone that aliases into broken stair-steps. They are not outlines. The only 'line-like' dark marks are shading ones: the drop line under each thatch tier lip, the 1px gaps between pier planks, and the vertical board seams on the red stall (about 15-20% darker than the board).
shading:
Shading is stylised Lambert: each material has 3-4 discrete tone bands, with an ordered dither across each band boundary, so it reads as about 6-8 steps. Gradients are never smooth.
Light: a high sun, about 60-70 deg elevation, coming slightly from the back-right of the screen.
- Top faces are brightest.
- Faces turned toward screen-right are about 10% darker (stall right wall #B1513D).
- Faces turned toward screen-left are about 20% darker (front wall #9E503C).
- Undersides and recesses drop to near-black.
Hue shift is strong. Shadows go cool and blue: orange wood shades into blue-grey #303E49 and then #161B20, and the shadow on the water is #54748A to #434D54. Highlights go warm yellow: grass tips #9BA168-#AEBA92, straw #E4D1A8 up to #FDF9EF.
Occlusion comes from the geometry, not SSAO:
- grass is dark at the base (#222D12) and light at the tip, so anything standing in it (chair legs, pots, bike wheels) looks sunk in;
- the stall interior under the eave is deep shadow;
- the deck darkens the posts beneath it.
Cast shadows are present but low in contrast and only slightly soft. The roof shades the counter. The pier throws a dark band onto the water beneath and in front of it, and this band merges with a dark, wobbly reflection of the posts and people. Shadow edges break up through the same dither, not a blur. No shadow or tint ever reaches the white background.
dithering:
The dithering is ordered (Bayer-style) and evaluated in screen space at art-pixel resolution, so the patterns look regular: checkerboards and cross-hatch grids, not random speckle.
1) Base-edge dissolve: a band about 6-12 art-px wide where coverage drops from 100% to 0. The surviving pixels sit on a regular checker or Bayer lattice and thin out toward the outside.
2) Tone transitions inside surfaces. On the water, the light 'sky reflection' patches (#88ABB8/#96B7C4 over #6F98AA) blend in through a visible 4x4 cross-hatch grid. Shadow edges on the water and grass break up the same way.
3) Ripples and highlights are drawn as 50% checker (2x2) bands of #B6C4C5/#D0DFE3 over the water, not as solid lines.
4) The thatch adds per-pixel hash speckle (about ±8% value) for straw fibre. This is texture rather than a dither pattern.
A 4x4 Bayer matrix (optionally 8x8 for the edge band) is enough everywhere. Index it by floor(gl_FragCoord.xy) of the low-res target, and compare a coverage or blend value against it with discard or step. Do not use blue noise and do not use animated noise: the lattice stays fixed on screen.
groundEdge:
The base has no thickness. There is no soil cross-section, no box sides, no plinth and no drop shadow. It is a flat ground patch (grass in one scene, water in the other) whose outline dissolves straight into pure white.
Shape:
- Stall: a rounded rectangle aligned to the iso axes, about 1.6:1. Its border is jagged by low-frequency fbm with an amplitude of about 3-5% of the patch size.
- Fishing: an organic blob, roughly an ellipse with irregular lobes, taken from a circle SDF plus fbm.
Mechanism to reproduce, applied in every ground-layer fragment shader (ground plane, grass blades, water plane):
1. Compute d = signed distance to the noisy outline in world XZ: sdRoundRect or circle, plus fbm(xz*freq)*amp.
2. Compute coverage = smoothstep(0.0, band, -d), with band equal to about 8-10 art-px in world units.
3. Discard if coverage <= bayer4x4(gl_FragCoord.xy). Use a strict comparison so the outermost lattice pixels thin out.
Grass adds a second, geometric layer. Blade instances are rejection-sampled with a probability that falls off over the same band, and blades are tall vertical streaks. Isolated blades therefore stick out below and beyond the edge, giving a ragged, hairy fringe (dark #606D50 tips and lighter dots scattered in the white).
Water adds a colour ramp. Inside the band, the colour also lerps toward a lighter, desaturated blue (#96B7C4 to #D0DFE3), so it pales just before it breaks into checker dots.
The background outside stays exactly #FFFFFF. Never alpha-blend a translucent fade: the output is always either full colour or pure white per pixel.
textures:
All micro-detail is procedural and sized to the art-pixel.

GRASS
- Grass is the defining feature: an extremely dense field of vertical 1-art-px-wide streaks, about one blade per pixel column, 4-10 art-px long, a few up to about 14.
- It completely hides the ground.
- Each blade runs from a dark base (#222D12/#344E1A) through #52652F and #68853A to a light tip (#9BA168, #AEBA92, occasionally dry #BBB276). Each blade gets a random value jitter of about ±15%, which gives the strong vertical striping.
- Shadowed blades drop one ramp step.
- Build it as an InstancedMesh of thin quads, not as a texture.

THATCH ROOF
- A low-pitch hipped or shed slab built from 2-3 stepped tiers. Each tier lip throws a 1px darker line (#9A774C).
- Surface: base #E4D1A8/#DED1A8 with mid tones #CDB78B and #C5AA79. Add anisotropic noise stretched along the slope (about 1:6) for straw bundles, occasional dark fibre strands (#B49B6D-#7A5835), and per-pixel speckle with rare near-white glints (#FDF9EF).
- The eave has a hanging fringe: an alpha-cut band of vertical stripes whose bottom ends are randomised per stripe (hash(floor(u*N))), darker (#C5AA79-#9A774C) and backlit.

WOOD
- Pier deck: separate plank boxes with 1px dark gaps, a per-plank colour jitter around #BF996A/#B7966F/#937252, and faint stretched-noise grain. The side faces fall to cool #303E49/#161B20.
- Stall walls: red boards #B1513D/#A25D46 with darker vertical seams every 3-4 art-px.

WATER
- Base #6F98AA/#759BAA.
- Slowly drifting fbm 'sky reflection' patches, quantized to 2-3 levels (#88ABB8, #96B7C4) with a Bayer cross-hatch.
- Ripple rings: thin elliptical 50% checker bands (#B6C4C5/#D0DFE3).
- Fish shadows: small dark slivers (#3E6282, about 6-10 x 2 art-px).
- Pier reflection: dark (#434D54/#54748A) and smeared vertically, with sine wobble.

SMALL PROPS
- Flat colour plus the same ramp: the white banner (#DFDFD2) with black kanji 氷 (draw it with a runtime CanvasTexture), terracotta pots #A25D46, jeans about #5A6E8C.
palette:
Natural, moderately desaturated, mostly mid to high value. HSV saturation is about 25-50%. Nothing is neon. The only near-blacks are cool shadow accents. The background is pure #FFFFFF (#FEFEFE measured).

Sampled hexes:
| Group | Colours |
|---|---|
| Grass | #222D12, #344E1A, #52652F, #68853A, #728E51, #7D9953, #9BA168, #AEBA92, dry #BBB276 |
| Thatch | #7A5835, #9A774C, #B49B6D, #C5AA79, #CDB78B, #DED1A8, #E4D1A8, #FDF9EF |
| Stall | red #B1513D / #A25D46 / #9E503C, interior #4F3428, banner #DFDFD2 / #D7D1BF |
| Denim / steel | #6D7C8C |
| Water | #3E6282 (fish), #54748A (shade), #6F98AA (base), #759BAA, #88ABB8, #96B7C4, #B6C4C5, #D0DFE3 (ripple / edge) |
| Pier shadow on water | #434D54 / #616E7A |
| Wood | #BF996A, #B7966F, #937252, side #303E49, deepest #161B20 |

Each material is defined as a 4-step ramp: cool dark, mid, light, warm highlight.

For a Tibetan gorshey scene, keep the same structure, for example:
- dry steppe grass ramp #2A3318 to #B8B27A;
- chuba robes in muted maroon #7A2E2A / #A4443A and ochre #C89A4A;
- prayer flags in desaturated #3E6E9E / #E8E2D0 / #B5463A / #5E8A4A / #D9B24A;
- white felt or stone #E6E0D2 with cool shadow #4A5560.
animation:
All motion is small, slow, and snapped to whole art-pixels by the low-res render.

Summer stall (7.2s loop):
- The seated man makes a gentle idle motion: torso, head and arm move 1-3 art-px, possibly fanning.
- Grass sways as a travelling wind wave. Blade tips shift by 1-2 art-px and bases stay fixed.
- Nothing else moves much. The fringe or banner may barely stir.

Fishing (12.4s loop):
- Concentric ripple rings spawn at the point where the line enters the water and near the posts. They expand to about 30-45 art-px radius while fading, with 2-3 rings per burst and a new burst every few seconds.
- 2-4 dark fish shadows glide under the surface along slow closed curves, heading along their path tangent.
- The light reflection patches drift slowly.
- The rod tip and line bob very slightly.
- The two seated figures are nearly still.

For a seamless loop, every motion must be a periodic function of phase p = t/L with integer frequencies:
- sin(2π·k·p + phase);
- ripple age = fract(p·n + offset);
- fish paths as Lissajous or closed splines with an integer lap count;
- looping noise sampled on a circle, e.g. fbm(xz + r·vec2(cos 2πp, sin 2πp)).
recipe: 1. Renderer and pixel target. new THREE.WebGLRenderer({antialias:false, alpha:false}), setPixelRatio(1), setClearColor(0xffffff,1), outputColorSpace = SRGBColorSpace, toneMapping = NoToneMapping. Render the scene into a WebGLRenderTarget of 384x384 (minFilter/magFilter = NearestFilter, depthBuffer true, generateMipmaps false). Blit it to a 1152x1152 canvas with a fullscreen-quad ShaderMaterial using texelFetch or nearest sampling, and set CSS image-rendering:pixelated. A simpler alternative is renderer.setSize(384,384,false) with a CSS-upscaled canvas.

2. Camera. Use THREE.OrthographicCamera sized so the diorama spans about 85% of the frame width. Place it at target + 100 * normalize(vec3(sin45*cos30, sin30, cos45*cos30)) and call lookAt(target). Lower the target slightly so there is about 25-30% white above the subject and about 15-20% below. Do not snap or move the camera.

3. Shared GLSL chunk. (a) bayer4(ivec2 p) returns a threshold in 0..1 from the 4x4 matrix [0,8,2,10; 12,4,14,6; 3,11,1,9; 15,7,13,5] / 16 + 1/32, indexed with floor(gl_FragCoord.xy) mod 4. (b) hash and valueNoise/fbm (3-4 octaves). (c) groundMask(vec2 xz): d = sdRoundRect(xz, halfSize, radius) for the stall or length(xz/ellipse) - 1 for the water blob, then d += fbm(xz*0.35)*amp; return smoothstep(0.0, uBand, -d) with uBand set to about 9 art-px in world units. (d) quantShade(float l, vec3 ramp[4]): idx = clamp(floor(l*3.0 + bayer4(...)), 0, 3), return ramp[idx]. The Bayer offset dithers every band boundary.

4. Lit material. Write one ShaderMaterial, or patch MeshLambertMaterial with onBeforeCompile. Compute lambert = max(dot(N, L), 0), with L = normalize(0.35, 1.0, -0.25): high and slightly back-right in screen terms. Add a small sky term of about 0.25, then multiply by the shadow factor from three's shadowmap chunks: use a DirectionalLight with castShadow, PCFSoftShadowMap and a 1024 shadow map, and set lights:true with the UniformsLib.lights uniforms. Feed the result into quantShade with a per-material 4-colour ramp (cool shadow, mid, light, warm highlight). Never write lerped smooth colours. Use flat shading or computeVertexNormals on low-poly primitives.

5. Ground patch. Use a PlaneGeometry rotated to XZ with a fragment shader where coverage = groundMask(vWorld.xz). Discard if coverage <= bayer4. Colour it dark grass #344E1A so gaps between blades read dark. There is no box underneath, no side faces, and nothing is drawn outside the mask.

6. Grass. Use an InstancedMesh of a single blade: a 2-triangle quad, width about 0.6 art-px in world units (so it rasterises to 1px at 384px), height 1, with its pivot at the base. Scatter 60-100k instances on a jittered grid. Accept an instance with probability groundMask(xz) + 0.15*noise so a sparse fringe survives past the edge. Give each instance random attributes: height of 4-10 art-px (a few up to 14), value jitter ±15%, and a slight yaw. In the vertex shader, add tip sway = h^2 * A * sin(2π(k*p) + dot(xz, windDir)*f) with A ≤ 1.5 art-px, k integer and p = t/L. Billboard the quad toward the camera azimuth so it is always 1px wide. In the fragment shader, colour from a base-to-tip gradient (#222D12 to #52652F to #9BA168/#AEBA92), multiply by the shadow factor (shadowed blades use #344E1A to #68853A), and also discard through groundMask plus Bayer at the very edge. Leave about 1.5 art-px of clear grass around object footprints only where needed. Otherwise let blades overlap object bases so props look sunk into the grass.

7. Stall props from primitives. Build the cart body from BoxGeometry with a red ramp [#4F3428, #9E503C, #B1513D, #C46A52] and a shader seam: darken 20% when fract(uv.x*nBoards) < 0.12. Add a counter and shelves of small boxes with coloured items. Add a white banner plane with 氷 drawn into a runtime CanvasTexture (NearestFilter), and thin cylinder poles. Build the bicycle from TorusGeometry wheels, thin cylinders for the frame and a wire box basket from LineSegments. The chair is thin boxes. Terracotta pots are LatheGeometry with ramp #6E3626/#A25D46. The man is boxes and capsules about 24 art-px tall: white tank top, blue jeans, skin tone. Animate his head and arm with small periodic rotations (±3-5 deg).

8. Thatch roof. Stack 2-3 slightly inset, sloped BoxGeometry tiers. In the fragment shader: base ramp [#9A774C, #C5AA79, #DED1A8, #FDF9EF]; fibre = valueNoise(vec2(along*60, across*10)); speck = hash(floor(gl_FragCoord.xy)) - 0.5; l += fibre*0.15 + speck*0.08 before quantShade; and darken 1px at each tier lip. Eave fringe: a PlaneGeometry strip along each eave edge, about 4-6 art-px tall. In its shader, stripe = floor(u*N), and discard if fract(u*N) > 0.7 or v < hash(stripe)*0.6. Colour it from the darker straw tones.

9. Water plane (fishing). The water ShaderMaterial uses coverage = groundMask(blob) and discards with Bayer. Then:
- Base #6F98AA.
- Reflection patches: r = fbm(xz*0.5 + loopCircle(p)*0.8), quantized to 3 levels (#6F98AA, #88ABB8, #96B7C4) via floor(r*3 + bayer4).
- Edge tint: mix toward #D0DFE3 by (1 - coverage)^2.
- Ripples: for each emitter c_i and n rings, age = fract(p*nBursts + off); ring = 1 - smoothstep(0, w, abs(length(xz - c) - age*Rmax)); if ring*(1 - age) > checker2x2, colour #D0DFE3/#B6C4C5.
- Fish: 3 ellipse SDFs on closed Lissajous paths with integer frequencies over L = 12.4 s, rotated to the path tangent; inside, apply #3E6282 where bayer < 0.7.
- Shadows: the shadow factor maps to #54748A/#434D54.
- Fake reflection: under the pier footprint, add dark vertical smears sampled with x += sin(z*8 + 2πp*2)*0.5 art-px.

10. Pier and figures. Use one BoxGeometry per plank with 1 art-px gaps and a per-instance colour jitter on the ramp [#161B20, #303E49, #937252, #BF996A]; the cool low end makes side faces go blue-black. Posts are dark cylinders. Two seated block figures. The fishing rod is a thin cylinder. The line is a THREE.Line along a quadratic sag curve (colour #2A3840, 1px, aliased), with its end bobbing as sin(2πp*k) at 1 art-px.

11. Optional unify pass. In the blit shader, before upscaling, apply per-channel posterize to about 20-24 levels with a Bayer offset to tie the colours together. Force any pixel with luminance > 0.97 to exact #FFFFFF so the background is never off-white. Do not add bloom, blur, vignette or outlines.

12. Loop and export. Use L = 7.2 s (stall) or 12.4 s (fishing) and p = (t % L)/L. Every animated term uses integer multiples of 2πp or fract(p*n). Every time-varying noise samples a circle in noise space, so frame L equals frame 0. For video, step a fixed dt (1/30) and capture frames with MediaRecorder on canvas.captureStream(30), or save PNG sequences. Keep motion amplitudes at 1-3 art-px so the pixel snapping stays readable rather than jittery.
